title: Short Stuff: Theme Park Cremations
summary: Short Stuff episode on what people do with cremated remains, focusing on scattering them in meaningful places. The hosts discuss "cremains" versus "cremated remains," the term "wildcat scattering" for scattering ashes against rules, and legal scattering in national parks and public waters (including a three-nautical-mile offshore guideline). They discuss the grossness question of ashes in lakes and boats, and then turn to Disney theme parks as a popular, but risky, spot for illicit scattering, citing a 2018 Wall Street Journal article and Disney's stated position that it does not happen. They conclude that ashes at Disney are typically swept up and thrown away, and close by advising against wildcat scattering.
topics: Pirates of the Caribbean ride ashes

segments.title: Cremains vs. cremated remains
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the term 'cremains,' note funeral directors prefer 'cremated remains,' and introduce the topic of what people do with ashes.

segments.title: Wildcat scattering
segments.summary: Hosts define 'wildcat scattering' as scattering ashes in defiance of rules, with a tangent on whether the term originated with HowStuffWorks writer Nathan Chandler and a driving-school 'wolf pack' anecdote.

segments.title: Legal scattering places and permits
segments.summary: Scattering is legal in national parks with a special permit and in public bodies of water with permission, often at a set distance from shore. For oceans, one source says three nautical miles offshore.

segments.title: Are cremated remains gross in water?
segments.summary: Hosts discuss why some people find ashes in lakes disgusting while others don't, noting that cremated remains are sterile ash exposed to high temperatures, and that the discomfort may come from their origin as a body, plus the practical problem of ash on a boat or shoe.

segments.title: Scattering ashes at Disney parks
segments.summary: Disney World and Disneyland are described as popular, though risky, wildcat scattering sites, especially Pirates of the Caribbean, It's a Small World, and The Haunted Mansion. Hosts cite a 2018 Wall Street Journal article and say Disney's official stance is that it does not happen, while staff report that ashes are swept up and trashed.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts joke about where they would want to be scattered and advise against wildcat scattering, then sign off.
